record.original_question: For increasing and decreasing tree families, especially recursive trees viewed as unordered increasing trees, can one determine the total number of parking functions or related aggregate quantities such as sums of parking functions, despite the fact that the differential equations produced by the current approach do not appear to have tractable solutions?

evidence.quote: (3) The problem of determining the total number of parking functions seems to be interesting for so-called increasing (or decreasing) tree families. For so-called recursive trees, i.e., unordered increasing trees, the approach presented could be applied, but the differential equations occurring do not seem to yield tractable solutions. For such tree families quantities such as the sums of parking functions as studied could be worthwhile treating as well.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A simple tree family on the vertex set $[n]=\{1,\dots,n\}$ is called an increasing tree family if every tree is rooted, the labels along any root-to-leaf path are strictly increasing, and the family is specified by a degree-weight generating function $\varphi(x)=\sum_{k\ge 0}\varphi_k x^k$ that assigns weight $\varphi_{d(v)}$ to a node of out-degree $d(v)$. Decreasing tree families are defined analogously with strictly decreasing labels. Recursive trees are the special case obtained by viewing increasing trees as unordered (i.e. children of a node form an unordered set), corresponding to $\varphi(x)=e^x$ in the exponential framework.

A parking function for a rooted labelled tree $T$ on $n$ vertices with $m\le n$ cars is a sequence $(s_1,\dots,s_m)\in V(T)^m$ of preferred parking spots such that the following process succeeds: car $i$ drives from $s_i$ toward the root, parking at the first unoccupied vertex it encounters; if all vertices on its path to the root are occupied, the process fails. The sequence is a parking function on $T$ when every car parks successfully. Let $P_{n,m}(T)$ denote the number of parking functions of length $m$ on $T$, and define the aggregate
$$ \mathcal{P}_{n,m}^{\mathcal{T}} \;=\; \sum_{T \in \mathcal{T}_n} w(T)\, P_{n,m}(T), $$
where $\mathcal{T}_n$ is the set of trees of size $n$ in a given increasing or decreasing tree family $\mathcal{T}$ and $w(T)$ is its combinatorial weight. One may also consider the sum-of-parking-function statistic $\sum_{(s_1,\dots,s_m)} (s_1+\cdots+s_m)$ summed over all parking functions of $T$, then averaged/summed over $\mathcal{T}_n$.

Problem. For increasing and decreasing tree families—and in particular for recursive trees (unordered increasing trees)—obtain a tractable determination of:
(a) the total number $\mathcal{P}_{n,m}^{\mathcal{T}}$ of parking functions, and
(b) related aggregate statistics such as the sums of parking-function values $\sum_T \sum_{(s_1,\dots,s_m)\in \mathrm{PF}(T)} (s_1+\cdots+s_m)$,
either by closed-form expressions, exact recursions, or asymptotic formulas (including possible phase-transition thresholds in $m/n$), despite the fact that the natural generating-function / differential-equation approach for recursive trees does not appear to yield directly solvable equations.
artifact.status_search_result: A recent survey on parking problems on random trees explicitly lists determining the total number of parking functions (and related aggregates such as sums of parking functions) for increasing/decreasing tree families—especially recursive trees—as an open problem, noting that the differential equations arising from the natural generating-function approach for recursive trees do not appear to have tractable solutions. No subsequent work resolving this question was located.

status_evidence.title: Short survey of results and open problems for parking problems on random trees
status_evidence.snippet: For recursive trees (i.e., unordered increasing trees), the approach presented could be applied, but the differential equations occurring do not seem to yield tractable solutions.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is stated as open in a recent survey.

status_evidence.title: Parking on the Random Recursive Tree
status_evidence.snippet: Parking on random recursive trees has been studied with phase transition results, but exact total parking-function counts for increasing tree families remain unaddressed.
status_evidence.claim: Related work addresses parking dynamics on recursive trees but not the aggregate counting problem.
